note: Curated journey register. J1, J4 and J8 were recovered: they are named in the header and test titles of e2e/tests/journeys.spec.ts, in two API integration test titles, and in the continuous-integration step that runs them. J2, J3, J5, J6 and J7 were empty rows implied by the numbering until 2026-08-26, when they were authored as product decisions under ADR 0007 — closing DOC-D-029. An authored journey lists no e2e spec until a spec names its identifier; the gate requires the identifier inside any spec listed here.

status_vocabulary.verified: Named in the repository and exercised end to end by a browser test that runs in continuous integration.
status_vocabulary.partial: The journey's steps ship and tests cover them, but no spec names the journey's identifier, so the register cannot claim it end to end.
status_vocabulary.planned: Authored under ADR 0007 with a statement and capabilities; some or all of its capabilities are registered intent, not shipped code.
status_vocabulary.unknown: Implied by numbering only. No source in the repository states what this journey is.

journeys.title: Capture a person in under a minute
journeys.statement: From anywhere in the application, the operator opens the capture line, types one line naming a person with an organization, tags, a date and a note, sees the parse previewed as chips, commits it, and finds the new record through the quick-switcher.
journeys.target: The whole journey completes within sixty seconds.
journeys.note: The sixty-second target is stated in the header of e2e/tests/journeys.spec.ts. The test asserts the steps complete, not the elapsed time, so the target is documented intent rather than an enforced budget.

journeys.title: Keep a valued tie warm
journeys.statement: The reconnect lane surfaces a tie drifting past its cadence; the operator opens the person, sees the history and why the tie ranks where it does, composes an outreach draft from real relationship facts, sends and logs it, and watches the strength recompute in the same sitting.
journeys.target: A drifting tie is noticed, understood, and re-engaged in one sitting, without the operator maintaining any list by hand.
journeys.note: Authored 2026-08-26 under ADR 0007; verified the same day when e2e/tests/exploration.spec.ts named the journey in the tests that walk it — reconnect lane on Today, interaction log with live strength recompute, ask with its factor decomposition, composer send-and-log.

journeys.title: Bring the past in without wrecking the graph
journeys.statement: The operator stages a LinkedIn or contacts export, reviews rows with per-row accept and skip and per-row subject assignment, commits the batch, works the duplicate queue on shared evidence, merges with an undo window, and can roll the whole batch back — ending with a graph that gained history without gaining a second self.
journeys.target: A first import lands as reviewed records with no silent duplicate surviving the first pass.
journeys.note: Authored 2026-08-26 under ADR 0007; verified the same day. exploration.spec.ts walks stage → commit → rollback and duplicate → merge → undo against the real stack; import.spec.ts and duplicates.spec.ts cover the review-screen states. Per-row subject assignment is exercised by unit coverage rather than a browser walk — recorded here so the claim stays inspectable.

journeys.title: Turn a job description into a tailored resume
journeys.statement: The operator opens the tailoring surface, starts a target session, pastes a job description, lets the parsed keywords score and select evidence against the one-page budget, and compiles a PDF.

journeys.title: Prove it with a dossier
journeys.statement: Facing a promotion review, a petition, or a reinvestigation, the operator selects the evidence records that carry the claim, chooses the audience template, and compiles a single-subject packet whose every claim cites its records, closed by a provenance appendix — from a graph that was already capturing the evidence as it happened.
journeys.target: A review-season packet that once took a weekend of archaeology compiles from already-captured evidence in under an hour.
journeys.note: Authored 2026-08-26 under ADR 0007 for the periodic-prover persona; verified 2026-08-27. dossier.spec.ts names the journey and walks it: the list naming each packet by the audience it is written for, a claim's marker resolving into the appendix entry that names its record and opens its revision trail, and the three audiences differing in what their sections demand. The walk that carries the journey is the third one, where a cited record is deleted and the packet is reopened: the citation still prints, marked withdrawn, and the document still compiles, which is the difference between a provenance appendix and a bibliography.

journeys.title: Leave with everything
journeys.statement: The operator exports the complete graph — every collection as JSON Lines, a Markdown vault readable anywhere, a checksummed manifest — verifies the checksums, restores the bundle on a fresh install with identity intact, and reads the vault in a plain-text editor with no Vitae anywhere in sight.
journeys.target: The bundle restores on a fresh install with document identity intact, and the vault reads in any plain-text editor.
journeys.note: Authored 2026-08-26 under ADR 0007. Export, checksums, and the sensitive-records boundary are named in e2e/tests/export.spec.ts; the restore half is exercised by the documented drill rather than a browser test, which is why the journey stays partial rather than verified.

journeys.title: See the correspondence truth
journeys.statement: The operator opens the correspondence rollup, sees reciprocity and reply-latency facts they could not have tallied by hand, finds the dormant-but-once-strong ties ranked with their evidence, picks one they would not have thought of, and steps into a warm re-introduction with the history in front of them.
journeys.target: The rollup names at least one dormant-but-once-strong tie the operator had not thought of, with the evidence to act on it.
journeys.note: Authored 2026-08-26 under ADR 0007; verified the same day, once interactions carried operator-stated direction. correspondence.spec.ts names the journey and walks it: the rollup's imbalance and recorded-broker registers, then the step into the person profile whose panel shows the same figures from the same function.

journeys.title: Recover a deleted record from trash
journeys.statement: The operator deletes a record, finds it in trash, restores it, and sees the record and the edges hidden with it return intact.
journeys.note: Also asserted at the API level by apps/api/src/__tests__/api.integration.test.ts, which records the soft-delete and restore operations.
